  1. Troubleshooting

Troubleshooting

First commands 

kubectl get inferenceservice -n models
kubectl get llminferenceservice -n models
kubectl get pods -n models
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n models | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
kubectl get events -n models --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30

Model pods have several containers. Inspect the right one:

kubectl logs <pod> -n models -c storage-initializer   # download phase
kubectl logs <pod> -n models -c kserve-container      # runtime
kubectl logs <pod> -n models -c queue-proxy           # request handling, when present

Helm install and template failures

Message Cause Fix
additional properties ... not allowed Unknown top-level key Check spelling; upstream keys go under dependency roots
found in Chart.yaml, but missing in charts/ Dependencies not built Run helm dependency build
cannot re-use a name that is still in use Release exists helm upgrade instead, or choose another name
no matches for kind "InferenceService" CRDs missing Enable the CRD components or install them first
rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists Another release owns the object Remove the old KServe installation or disable overlapping components

Validate values against the schema without a cluster:

helm template model-serving helm-charts/model-serving -f values.yaml > /dev/null

A setting has no effect

Two frequent causes:

  1. Upstream values at the wrong root. Helm does not forward parent values into subcharts.
# Ignored
kserve:
  controller:
    gateway:
      ingressGateway:
        className: contour

# Correct
kserve-resources:
  kserve:
    controller:
      gateway:
        ingressGateway:
          className: contour

  1. A field the chart does not render. models entries support the fields in Inference services and llmInferenceServices entries those in LLM inference services. A key outside those lists is accepted by the schema but ignored by the template.

  2. An explicit containers block. Setting containers under template, worker, or prefill.template replaces the generated container for that pool, so image, args, resources, and automatic HF_TOKEN injection no longer apply there.

Confirm what was actually produced:

helm get manifest model-serving -n kserve | grep -A30 'kind: InferenceService'

Pod stays in Init

The storage initializer is still downloading.

kubectl logs <pod> -n models -c storage-initializer -f
Message Cause Fix
401 / 403 Token missing or license not accepted See Hugging Face
404 Wrong URI Verify the hf://org/repo or bucket path
Slow progress Large model Expected; consider Local model cache
no such host Egress blocked or DNS failure Check network policy and DNS
AccessDenied Storage credentials wrong Verify Secret and ServiceAccount

Pod stays Pending 

kubectl describe pod <pod> -n models | sed -n '/Events/,$p'
Message Fix
Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu Free GPUs, add nodes, or lower the request
Insufficient memory Lower resources.requests or add capacity
untolerated taint Add tolerations; see GPU and scheduling
pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims Create the PVC or fix the storage class

CrashLoopBackOff 

kubectl logs <pod> -n models -c kserve-container --previous --tail=100
Cause Signal Fix
GPU out of memory CUDA out of memory Lower --max-model-len or --gpu-memory-utilization; use a larger GPU
Host out of memory Exit code 137, OOMKilled Raise resources.limits.memory
Shared memory too small Bus error, shm failures Raise shmSize or devShm.sizeLimit
Bad arguments unrecognized arguments Check args against the runtime’s flags
Wrong format Model loader errors Match modelFormat to the artifact
Missing GPU driver no CUDA-capable device Verify the device plugin on the node

CreateContainerConfigError

Almost always a missing Secret or key.

kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models
kubectl get secret hf-secret -n models -o jsonpath='{.data.HF_TOKEN}' | head -c 8

The key must be exactly HF_TOKEN, and the Secret must exist in the workload namespace, not the release namespace.

READY is False but pods run 

kubectl describe inferenceservice <name> -n models
Condition Meaning Fix
RuntimeNotRecognized Runtime name wrong or disabled kubectl get clusterservingruntime
NoSupportingRuntime Format not advertised by any runtime Set runtime and modelFormat explicitly
PredictorConfigurationError Invalid predictor spec Review rendered manifest
Ingress not ready Gateway missing See Networking and endpoints

Check the runtime’s advertised formats:

kubectl get clusterservingruntime kserve-sklearnserver -o jsonpath='{.spec.supportedModelFormats}' | jq

Requests fail

Status Cause Fix
Connection refused Pod not ready kubectl get pods -n models
404 Wrong path or model name curl /v1/models to list names
503 Backend unavailable Check readiness and route targets
400 Payload shape wrong Match the runtime’s protocol
Timeout Model still loading, or request too large Watch logs; raise client timeout

Webhook errors 

Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook "inferenceservice.kserve-webhook-server.validator"

kubectl get pods -n kserve
kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration | grep kserve
kubectl get certificate -n kserve
kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=100

Causes include the controller not running, cert-manager not installed, or an expired webhook certificate.

Controller not starting 

kubectl describe pod -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager
kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=200
Cause Fix
cert-manager missing Install cert-manager, then upgrade
Shared resources missing Ensure one chart sets createSharedResources: true
RBAC conflicts Remove leftovers from a previous KServe installation
Image pull failure Add pull secrets or mirror the image

Duplicate or conflicting resources 

helm list -A | grep -i kserve
kubectl get crd | grep kserve.io
kubectl get clusterservingruntime

Two releases installing KServe will fight over cluster-scoped objects. Keep one owner; see Components.

Collecting diagnostics 

NS=models
kubectl get all -n $NS > diag-resources.txt
kubectl describe inferenceservice -n $NS > diag-isvc.txt
kubectl describe llminferenceservice -n $NS > diag-llmisvc.txt
kubectl get events -n $NS --sort-by=.lastTimestamp > diag-events.txt
kubectl logs -n kserve -l control-plane=kserve-controller-manager --tail=500 > diag-controller.txt
helm get values model-serving -n kserve > diag-values.yaml

helm get values can include a token supplied through hfSecret.token. Remove secrets before sharing diagnostics.
